    {"id": "K1.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "A command-line user runs the tool with CSV files."},
    {"id": "K1.2", "basis": "S1", "answer": "Printed totals match the sales records."},
    {"id": "K2.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "CSV summary and tests; no other product features."},
    {"id": "K2.2", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Empty repository; discover any environment behavior requiring preservation."},
    {"id": "K3.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "CSV paths; region, product, unit_price, units; three printed sections."},
    {"id": "K3.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Exit 0 on success, 2 for input errors, 1 otherwise."},
    {"id": "K4.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Aggregate all supplied files; revenue equals unit price times units."},
    {"id": "K4.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Reject missing fields, negative values, invalid prices or noninteger units."},
    {"id": "K5.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Process-local aggregates last only for the command invocation."},
    {"id": "K5.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Output goes to caller; restart recomputes; concurrent edits unsupported."},
    {"id": "K6.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use available Python 3; discover its exact version."},
    {"id": "K6.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use Python standard library; no third-party dependencies."},
    {"id": "K6.3", "basis": "default", "answer": "One or more CSV paths as positional arguments; no configuration."},
    {"id": "K7.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Separate CSV parsing, aggregation, formatting, and command-line entry."},
    {"id": "K8.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use unittest; run python -m unittest discover."},
    {"id": "K8.2", "basis": "S2", "answer": "Tests invoke the command and verify printed aggregates and errors."},
    {"id": "K9.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Deliver in source checkout; local Python and file access required."},
    {"id": "K10.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Use decimal arithmetic; clear text output; no additional bounds assumed."},
    {"id": "K11.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Actual CSV schema or revenue rules differ from assumptions."},
    {"id": "K11.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Representative CSV evidence or an early command-boundary test exposes mismatch."}

  "summary": "S1 [fact]: A command-line user needs printed total revenue, revenue by region, and units by product from sales CSV files; the named delivery target is a Python command-line tool. S2 [fact]: Automated tests must cover the requested behavior. Repository and run boundary [fact]: The repository is empty; this unattended intake implements nothing and has no tools or files. Authority [fact]: The request grants delivery of the tool in the source checkout, not deployment to an unnamed target. Visibility [fact]: An isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome would exist only after release, which is not requested. Interaction and state [default]: This is a noninteractive command; the operating system identifies the caller, aggregates remain in process memory until exit, and output is visible to the caller and anyone with access to its destination. No shared application state, cross-session persistence, or concurrency control is assumed; these defaults rule out shared dashboards and coordinated live updates. Discovery must establish available runtime facilities before relying on them. Input and domain question [recorded default; blocks implementation and acceptance checks]: After discovery checks for representative records and applicable domain guidance, assume one or more UTF-8 CSV paths with a header containing region, product, unit_price, and units; prices are nonnegative decimal amounts, units are nonnegative integers, and revenue is unit_price multiplied by units. Reject missing fields and invalid or negative values; aggregate all supplied files. A header-only file contributes zero. Output and error question [recorded default; blocks boundary checks]: After discovery establishes any existing output conventions, print clearly labeled total, per-region, and per-product sections to stdout; report input errors to stderr with exit 2, unexpected failures with exit 1, and success with exit 0. Runtime and test question [discovery, then recorded default; blocks implementation and test execution]: First establish the available Python version and invocation environment; assume Python 3, standard-library dependencies, unittest, and python -m unittest discover. Delivery naming question [discovery, then recorded default; blocks a concrete entry-point name]: First check for workspace conventions; otherwise choose and document a descriptive script name in the checkout. Source hints [unverified leads]: The request itself, any representative sales CSVs or workspace conventions found during discovery, and Python documentation; no team, channel, internal site, private repository, owner, or sensitive locator was supplied. Risk [assumption]: A mismatched CSV schema or revenue rule could invalidate the summary; representative data and early command-boundary tests should expose that risk."
}
